title: The microscope
summary: The modern light microscope goes back to sometime between 1590 and 1618, when the Dutch spectacle maker Zacharias Janssen made an early one with several lenses in a tube. In 1665 Robert Hooke described what he called cells in a piece of cork. Antonie van Leeuwenhoek improved the instrument further, and in 1700 made the first description of a cell nucleus.

uncertainty.note: Zacharias and Hans Janssen created early multiple-lens tubes in Middelburg c. 1590–1600; biological breakthroughs followed with Hooke's description of cells in 1665 and Leeuwenhoek's observations of microorganisms through the 1670s–1700.

importance.justification: The invention of the compound microscope and subsequent single-lens designs revealed the cellular basis of life and the microbial world, revolutionizing biology and medicine.
